title: Casper and the Lantern
premise: In the winter of 1899, Hazel Thornbury, a widowed lighthouse keeper on the Cornish coast, tends his light and his late wife's unfinished lantern workshop while the fiercest storms in a generation batter the cliffs. When a sealed letter washes ashore implicating the neighboring family who took him in after his wife's death in a smuggling plot, Hazel must choose between loyalty to his found family and the truth that could save a village boy from hanging. As the century turns and the workshop floods, Hazel completes his wife's final lantern design, exposes the true smugglers, and finally allows himself to belong again.
about_author: Lior Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the English coast. Their fiction draws on the weathered voices of those records to explore quiet lives caught in loud histories.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He climbs the tower through sleet, tending the light and avoiding the Christmas gathering at the Penhale farm below. Flashback fragments of his wife Maren's death two years prior establish his grief and self-imposed isolation. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. After the first great storm, he walks the tideline and finds a waterproof oilskin packet: a sealed letter addressed to no one, marked with the Penhales' crest. He pockets it without opening it, telling himself it's none of his affair. Beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Family That Fed Him
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV at the Penhale farmhouse dinner. Warm scenes with matriarch Bess Penhale, her son Tom, and grandson Wynn, the boy who idolizes him. The letter burns in Hazel's pocket. Beat: belonging offered, guilt accepted alongside it.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Design
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV in the cliffside workshop, where Maren's half-built storm lantern sits under dust sheets. Her journal reveals she was designing a lens that could signal ships past the reef. He begins finishing it as an act of mourning. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Letter, Opened
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, night scene. Unable to sleep, he breaks the seal. The letter names Tom Penhale as party to a wrecking scheme—luring a merchant ship onto the reef—with payment promised by a man called Corvus. Beat: the floor drops out of his world.

chapters.title: Wynn's Questions
chapters.summary: Wynn's POV. The fourteen-year-old shadows Hazel on the cliffs, chattering about becoming a keeper himself. His innocent trust makes Hazel's secret unbearable. A near-fall on wet rock forces Hazel to catch him—and admit he cares. Beat: love as liability.

chapters.title: Corvus Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A smooth-talking stranger arrives at the village inn asking about 'salvage rights.' Hazel observes him courting Tom's debts. He realizes the plot is real and ongoing, aimed at the spring convoy. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Bess Knows More Than She Says
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel/Bess POV. Bess finds Hazel studying old charts and deflects with stories of hard winters. A single line—'Tom's father drowned saving men from a wrecked ship'—hints the family has history with false lights. Beat: suspicion entangled with tenderness.

chapters.title: Half-Finished Work
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Progress on Maren's lantern stalls; its prism assembly defeats him. He rereads her journal and finds a page torn out. Meanwhile Tom asks Hazel to keep the light burning 'extra bright' on certain nights—innocently, he claims. Beat: every kindness now reads twice.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Path
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, tense night reconnaissance. Following Corvus's man through fog, Hazel discovers a cache in a sea cave: signal lamps, rope, and a duplicate of Maren's torn journal page—she had discovered the original wrecking ring before she died. Beat: horror that grief and conspiracy share a root.

chapters.title: A Choice of Silences
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He drafts a letter to the harbormaster, then burns it—naming Tom would orphan Wynn and destroy Bess. He decides instead to finish Maren's lantern, whose unique lens could prove which light lured ships. Beat: loyalty chosen over truth, temporarily.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Wynn's POV. The great storm of the season is forecast; the village battens down. Tom grows secretive, missing meals. Corvus's crew quietly provisions the cave. Beat: converging forces under darkening skies.

chapters.title: The Night of False Light
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax of act two. During the storm's peak, someone shows a light from the wrong headland; a coaster founders on the reef. Hazel saves two sailors but sees, across the water, the silhouette of the second lamp—and recognizes the workshop's own spare lens. Beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: Accusations
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The harbormaster arrives; suspicion falls on the nearest keepers—the Penhales. Bess lies to protect Tom; Tom cannot meet Hazel's eyes. Wynn overhears everything and runs into the rain. Beat: the found family cracking under weight.

chapters.title: Wynn Runs
chapters.summary: Wynn's POV. The boy takes refuge in the sea cave and discovers Corvus's men moving the evidence—and hears them name Tom as their fall man. He races to tell Hazel but collapses with fever on the way. Beat: innocence armed with terrible knowledge.

chapters.title: Fever Watch
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He nurses Wynn through the night while the boy deliriously repeats what he heard. Bess keeps vigil too; between them, unspoken, they both know now. Tom confesses to his mother offstage—we see only Bess's face afterward. Beat: truth arriving through love's back door.

chapters.title: Tom's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Tom's POV, the novel's most vulnerable chapter. He explains the debt, the coercion, the one night he held the lamp before his nerve broke. He begs Hazel not to let Wynn learn of it from anyone else. Beat: shame met, not excused.

chapters.title: The Lens Completed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Using the recovered journal page, Hazel solves Maren's prism problem and finishes the lantern as the equinox gales begin. Its beam cuts clean and unmistakable—a signature no imitator can fake. Beat: the dead wife's work becomes the living proof.

chapters.title: Corvus's Gambit
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Corvus, sensing exposure, plans one last wreck during the equinox storm and intends to burn the cave cache—and the workshop—with it. Hazel learns via Wynn's eavesdropping. Beat: stakes narrowed to what can be saved.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Hazel/Wynn POV. In the worst storm of the year, Hazel lights Maren's lantern in the workshop window to counter Corvus's false light, guiding the convoy clear while Wynn rides for the revenue cutter. The workshop floods and partially collapses around him; he holds the light anyway. Corvus is taken in the surf. Beat: sacrifice completing the work.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The workshop is ruined but the lantern survived; the harbor court clears the Penhales of the foundering, with Tom testifying against Corvus and accepting his sentence. Bess tells Hazel he was family long before the letter. Beat: truth and loyalty reconciled at cost.

chapters.title: A Light With Two Names
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue in spring. The rebuilt workshop bears a new sign: Thornbury & Penhale. Wynn begins his apprenticeship; Maren's lantern burns in the tower beside Hazel's own. He writes her name in the keeper's log at last. Beat: belonging chosen, grief carried forward, home made.
